title: Steal Like an Artist: Who I'm Stealing From and Why
body:
Not long ago, while looking for books to read, I stumbled upon *Steal Like an Artist* by Austin Kleon.

I thought it was a masterpiece. I had already been practicing a lot of the advice without ever thinking of it as a documented method.

The core idea of the book,  and the talk,  is to find people who have done the things you want to do, people you admire, and copy their style while transforming it and making it your own. So that other people can steal from you too.

So after giving it some thought, I decided to be more systematic about the method and set up a list of mentors I'm stealing from, and why I chose them.

I made my choices based on what I want to learn and an "engineering excellence" note I read not long ago, which describes the skills and attributes of a great engineer. As I list who I chose, you'll also see what those attributes are.

---

## Andrej Karpathy

**What I'm stealing:** Engineering excellence + technical communication

One of the first people I followed once I decided to switch into tech. I've taken his courses, watched his videos, read his blogs — and I think he is brilliant. His mastery of the field is admirable.

## Chip Huyen

**What I'm stealing:** Technical communication, learning in public

If you were interested in machine learning at any point, you've heard of her. Besides being one of the best in the field, she is very open about her growth trajectory and how she started teaching ML systems design because she actually wanted to learn it for example.

Her books are probably the most famous in ML/AI, and she communicates exceptionally well. I want to copy that.

## Jeff Dean

**What I'm stealing:** Debugging + coding + stewardship + engineering excellence

If you ask me what engineer I want to be like, it's no other than Jeff Dean. I just love how much he cares, and how much fun he has talking and working in the field. His prowess is known by all — and being interested in AI/ML and infra, I always end up running into a paper, a blog, or a video of his whenever I'm trying to learn about engineering and computer systems. He's accomplished exceptional things and I want to study his ways and try to put them into practice.

## Barack Obama

**What I'm stealing:** Direction + leadership

Who's a better role model than the only Black man to become president of the United States — and do an amazing job at it, while being funny, classy, and still a great husband and dad? He is a hero of mine. His leadership style is one I admire a lot.

## Alex Hormozi

**What I'm stealing:** Work ethic + brutal self-honesty

I find myself always agreeing with his takes, and practicing what he preaches led me to land my job at Meta. If I was to choose somebody else here, it would be Garyvee — but Hormozi won because he also likes going to the gym like me, which I thought gave us more in common. Still love Gary though.

## Patrick Collison

**What I'm stealing:** Technical communication + engineering depth

He was actually recommended by AI. Once I had chosen all the others, I asked if there was one person I should add based on the people I already had, and Collison was the only recommendation. I read his whole website that same night, and I really like his ideas.
